pages.title: A Practical Guide to Planning 2BHK Home Interiors | Akruthi
pages.h1: A thoughtful start to planning your 2BHK interiors
pages.description: A practical checklist for planning a 2BHK home: priorities, room uses, storage, measurements and questions for a designer.
pages.intro: Before collecting finishes and furniture ideas, spend a little time understanding what your home needs to do. A useful brief makes the next design conversation more focused.
sections: Write down your priorities
Separate essentials from nice-to-haves. Think about daily routines, work, guests and any upcoming changes.
Measure and document
Record room dimensions, doors, windows, columns and fixed services. Photos of each wall are useful context.
Plan storage with the room
List what needs to be stored and where you reach for it. This helps make storage useful rather than simply large.
Set a realistic scope
Decide which rooms to address now, note your budget range if known, and ask how scope choices affect the proposal.
Collect references selectively
Save a few examples that explain what you like. Add a note about the specific quality you want to borrow.
Talk through the details
Ask about design stages, materials, responsibilities, approvals and how changes are handled. Each provider's process will differ.

sections: Describe your routine
How many people cook? What kinds of meals do you make? Do you prep in batches? These answers shape the priorities.
Map appliances and services
Note appliance sizes and existing water, gas and electrical points. Confirm what can be changed with the relevant professionals.
Think through storage
List cookware, groceries and small appliances. Keep frequent-use items easy to access.
Compare work surfaces and fronts
Ask about care, cleaning and suitability for your pattern of use, alongside appearance.
Review movement
A plan should leave comfortable room to open doors and drawers and move between work areas.
Confirm the scope
Clarify what the proposal covers, which selections are included and how installation details are agreed.

pages.title: How to Plan Home Lighting for Everyday Living | Akruthi
pages.h1: Layering light for comfortable everyday living
pages.description: Learn how ambient, task and accent lighting can support different activities and moods around your home.
pages.intro: Lighting can make a room useful at different times of day. Start by observing the daylight and tasks in each area, then plan a considered mix of sources.
sections: Begin with daylight
Notice when direct sun enters, which corners remain dim and where glare can be uncomfortable.
Identify the tasks
Reading, cooking, grooming and working each need appropriate illumination in the right place.
Add comfortable general light
Ambient lighting helps you move through and use a room. Consider control and flexibility.
Use accent light sparingly
A focused beam can highlight art, texture or a feature, but should support the room rather than compete with it.
Coordinate early
Lighting positions interact with furniture, ceilings and electrical planning. Review them together during design.

pages.title: Questions to Ask Before Hiring an Interior Designer | Akruthi
pages.h1: Questions to ask before choosing an interior designer
pages.description: A useful list of questions about scope, design stages, materials, estimates, responsibilities and communication for your home project.
pages.intro: Choosing a design partner is easier when you understand how a project will work. Use these questions to compare proposals on the details that matter to you.
sections: What is included in the scope?
Ask which rooms, drawings, services, products and site activities the proposal covers.
How are decisions and changes handled?
Understand how selections are approved and how changes may affect the cost or schedule.
How are materials specified?
Ask how products, finishes and alternatives are documented.
Who coordinates the work?
Clarify roles, communication channels and who to contact with questions.
What is the payment and estimate structure?
Request a clear written proposal and understand any exclusions before proceeding.
Can I see relevant completed work?
Review authentic examples and ask what parts of the project the designer delivered.
